# SK0218 — The boolean member tests can use a property pattern

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`skala arrange` combines boolean member checks on the same non-null receiver into a property pattern.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Formatting |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | 8.0 |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

A condition such as `!rule.Retired && rule.RequiresSemantics` describes one object state. A property pattern expresses that state together, while retaining each member name and its required boolean value.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (!rule.Retired && rule.RequiresSemantics) { Run(); }
```

Write:

```csharp
if (rule is { Retired: false, RequiresSemantics: true }) { Run(); }
```

## When it does not fire

The receiver must be a stable local, a non-ref parameter, or this, with non-null flow state for reference types. Only boolean fields and nonvirtual compiler-generated property getters qualify, because pattern matching may reorder member reads. Nullable or dynamic receivers, repeated members, volatile fields, custom getters, expression trees, comments within the condition and formatter-off regions are left alone. The rule requires a semantic model and C# 8 or later.
